prompt:
The spool drawings go to the prefabrication shop on Friday, so this sheet is plotted and taped down for the material check.

One process drawing lies flat on the plotting bench. A single main line runs right across it from edge to edge, at a plotted 48 metres overall, and that figure is boxed in the sheet corner with the material table. The table names carbon steel, stainless and a chrome-moly alloy, and gives each of them its own pen style. Sitting on the run are a gate valve, a check valve and a flanged joint at either end of a strainer spool, each drawn to the house symbol. The house rule printed under the table is that a change of material may be made only at a fitting, never in a plain run of pipe.

Which material each stretch of the line is drawn in, and where each stretch begins, is what the table does not say.
easy_question: Does this picture show a process drawing taped flat on a bench with one long pipe line running right across it and valve and flange symbols sitting on that line? Answer yes or no only.

steps.ask: Follow the main line across the sheet from left to right and watch the pen style it is drawn in. Answer with one of: every change of pen style sits at a valve or flange symbol; at least one change sits in a plain run with no symbol at it; the pen style never changes across the whole sheet.

steps.target: unbroken stretches of the main line drawn in one pen style
